statusDetail: Coverage-complete agentic audit of seven representative paths; playback, authenticated history, payment/subscription and post-login account management were excluded because they require consent, credentials or commercial commitment.

page.framework: Server-rendered multi-page application with deferred client-side JavaScript
page.notes: Public Spanish media/listing site. Raw HTML retains 87% of rendered content. A consent overlay is present on fresh desktop sessions.

paths.description: Homepage and primary discovery surface; represents global navigation, consent, recommendations, search entry, theming, performance and security.
Homepage at a 360x800 mobile viewport; represents narrow-screen layout, reflow and touch use.
Weekly best listing; represents ranked/listing templates. Other category and search result lists were not duplicated because they share the card/navigation shell.
Category index; represents taxonomy navigation and content browsing.
Representative public video detail page; covers the core content destination and share metadata. Playback itself was not started to avoid unnecessary media transfer.
Signup/account entry flow; email branch and empty submission exercised to inspect labels, autocomplete, disclosure and error recovery.
Deliberate unknown route; represents HTTP/application recovery and navigation back to useful content.

findings.summary: Reduced-motion preference does not suppress loading animation
findings.evidence: With prefers-reduced-motion: reduce active, the evaluate probe found eight running 2,000 ms shimmer animations and no prefers-reduced-motion CSS rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Disable non-essential shimmer and transition animation inside @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce).

findings.summary: Page-to-page navigation swaps abruptly
findings.evidence: CSS inspection across the homepage styles found no view-transition rules, while the primary journey crosses full document routes.
findings.suggestedFix: Add cross-document View Transitions for same-origin listing, detail and account navigation, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: Persistent navigation does not respond to scroll state
findings.evidence: The full homepage is over 4,500 CSS px tall, but stylesheet inspection found no scroll-state or scroll-timeline support and the header remains static chrome.
findings.suggestedFix: Use CSS scroll-state container queries or a restrained shrinking header/progress affordance on long listings.

findings.summary: Cookie consent obscures the primary content on every fresh desktop path
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshots of the homepage, detail and signup show a large centered consent overlay covering the page before interaction. Reject is available and equally prominent, but the interruption still dominates the initial task.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce the consent surface, preserve access to context, and avoid re-presenting it once a choice is stored.

findings.summary: Consent overlay is not exposed through a semantic dialog primitive
findings.evidence: DOM inspection found no dialog element and no role=dialog while the screenshot shows a modal-like overlay.
findings.suggestedFix: Implement the consent flow with <dialog> and correct modal focus management, or an equivalent correctly named dialog role when native dialog cannot be used.

findings.summary: Mobile viewport renders a 1024 px desktop canvas
findings.evidence: At a 360x800 viewport, layout evidence reported scrollWidth 1024, clientWidth 360 and 664 px horizontal overflow; the screenshot clips the main feed behind the fixed-width sidebar.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the fixed desktop canvas with an intrinsic mobile layout, collapse/off-canvas the sidebar, and verify scrollWidth equals visual viewport width.

findings.summary: Components do not adapt at their container boundary
findings.evidence: Rendered stylesheet inspection found no @container rules, and the card/sidebar composition remains desktop-sized in the narrow capture.
findings.suggestedFix: Use container-type and size-aware component queries for cards, navigation and sidebar composition, retaining a viewport fallback where necessary.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is not visibly indicated on the first navigation link
findings.evidence: After programmatically focusing the first visible link, computed style was outline: none and box-shadow: none. Lighthouse also reported accessibility failures.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a high-contrast :focus-visible ring for all links and controls, and verify the complete keyboard path.

findings.summary: Lab LCP misses the good threshold
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP at 3,566.8 ms (performance 0.90), above the 2.5 s good threshold. A separate warm trace measured 1,619.6 ms, so the issue is condition-sensitive rather than universal.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the actual LCP candidate, reduce document latency and validate on cold mobile runs and field data.

findings.summary: Critical delivery starts with many stylesheets and a large request graph
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 141 requests and 1.67 MB transferred. Three parser-inserted high-priority stylesheets were render-blocking candidates; DOM confirmation shows scripts are deferred but styles are in head.
findings.suggestedFix: Inline only critical CSS, defer non-critical page/chunk styles, and shorten the initial dependency graph.

findings.summary: JavaScript dominates the initial transfer
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 61 script requests transferring 1,014,569 bytes; the index bundle alone transferred 401,971 bytes and Google sign-in added 98,496 bytes before signup interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Split the index bundle by feature, load authentication code only at intent, and use coverage analysis to remove unused/duplicate modules.

findings.summary: Interactive controls lack accessible names
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found two button-name and two link-name failures; the DOM probe counted 52 interactive elements without visible text or common naming attributes. The email branch also exposes duplicate email inputs without associated labels.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every control a programmatic name, associate labels with signup fields, and remove duplicate or hidden focusable email inputs.

findings.summary: Text and controls fail minimum contrast
findings.evidence: Lighthouse identified 13 color-contrast failures and produced an accessibility score of 0.72.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust foreground/surface tokens to meet WCAG AA in both themes and verify disabled, muted and advertising labels.

findings.summary: Focus visibility is insufficient despite otherwise sensible landmarks
findings.evidence: The page has main, nav, header and footer landmarks and a valid heading order, but the focused first navigation link has no visible outline or shadow.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply consistent :focus-visible styling and run a keyboard focus-order walkthrough across menus, consent and signup.

findings.summary: Narrow-screen reflow fails
findings.evidence: The 360 px capture retains a 1024 px layout and 664 px overflow, so zoom/reflow users cannot access a coherent single-column reading order.
findings.suggestedFix: Rebuild the shell with fluid/intrinsic sizing and test at 320 CSS px and 400% zoom without two-dimensional scrolling.

findings.summary: Image sizing and delivery metadata are incomplete
findings.evidence: The image audit found 29 of 36 images without width/height, 12 oversized images, eight below-fold images not lazy-loaded and one missing alt.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit width and height or aspect-ratio for every media card, select correctly sized srcset candidates and lazy-load below-fold images.

findings.summary: Localized pages omit hreflang and a discoverable sitemap signal
findings.evidence: The Spanish homepage has a canonical URL and 200 status, but the DOM has zero hreflang links, robots.txt declares no Sitemap line, and /sitemap.xml returned an empty response.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish locale-specific hreflang alternates and a valid sitemap index referenced from robots.txt.

findings.summary: Video detail page lacks VideoObject structured data
findings.evidence: The representative detail exposes useful Open Graph video metadata but contains no JSON-LD block, leaving the rich entity less explicit to crawlers.
findings.suggestedFix: Add schema.org VideoObject JSON-LD that matches the visible title, thumbnail, duration, upload date and canonical URL.

findings.summary: Cookies and CSP do not provide a strong secure baseline
findings.evidence: HTTPS and HSTS are present, but x_csrf_token and settings are not Secure, settings uses SameSite=None, and CSP is limited to frame-ancestors rather than controlling script/style sources.
findings.suggestedFix: Mark all HTTPS cookies Secure, justify or remove SameSite=None, and deploy a nonce/hash-based CSP that constrains active content.

findings.summary: Third-party and analytics traffic starts before consent choice
findings.evidence: The initial HAR recorded 117 third-party requests and 1.56 MB from 15 origins while the cookie choice overlay was still present, including collector.xhamster.com and tsyndicate.com traffic.
findings.suggestedFix: Block non-essential analytics, advertising and identity resources until affirmative consent; reduce and batch necessary telemetry.

findings.summary: Signup does not offer a visible phishing-resistant sign-in path
findings.evidence: The exercised signup offers Google, X and email/password. The email password uses autocomplete=new-password, but no visible passkey/WebAuthn option was present.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer passkey registration and sign-in alongside federated and recovery paths, requesting it only from explicit user intent.

findings.summary: Defensive response headers are incomplete
findings.evidence: HSTS and clickjacking protection pass, but X-Content-Type-Options and Referrer-Policy are absent; Permissions-Policy only advertises client-hint delegation.
findings.suggestedFix: Add nosniff, a restrictive Referrer-Policy and an explicit least-privilege Permissions-Policy; consider Trusted Types for this script-heavy surface.

findings.summary: Email signup disables useful autofill
findings.evidence: The email branch exposes duplicate text inputs named email with autocomplete=off; only the password uses autocomplete=new-password.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a single type=email input with autocomplete=email and a proper label; retain new-password on the password field.

findings.summary: Thumbnail assets are often oversized or missing responsive metadata
findings.evidence: The image audit found 12 images over twice their display width, 29 missing intrinsic dimensions, three without srcset and 16 reported in legacy formats.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve right-sized AVIF/WebP responsive candidates, reserve aspect ratio and avoid fetching 530 px thumbnails for roughly 194 px slots.

findings.summary: Background collection and advertising work is loaded eagerly
findings.evidence: The initial network capture made 141 requests, including collector and advertising calls before the visitor selected a cookie preference.
findings.suggestedFix: Gate optional work on consent and intent, batch analytics, and defer background fetches until the page is idle and visible.

findings.summary: Third parties consume most of the initial page budget
findings.evidence: Third-party origins transferred 1,559,569 of 1,667,337 bytes (about 94%) before any video playback; scripts account for about 1.01 MB.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party byte/request budget, lazy-load identity and advertising integrations, and retain media deferral until explicit playback.

taskList.title: Rebuild the mobile shell for true reflow
Gate third-party traffic on consent and enforce a byte budget
Fix accessible names, labels, contrast and keyboard focus
Harden cookies, CSP and browser security policies
Reduce critical CSS and initial JavaScript
Use semantic, less obstructive consent UI
Correct image sizing and responsive delivery
Add locale indexing and VideoObject metadata
Improve signup autofill and add passkeys

checkOutcomes.method: Paired screenshots under prefers-color-scheme light and dark
checkOutcomes.evidence: Light and dark emulation produced coherent, deliberately different light/dark surfaces and readable consent controls.

checkOutcomes.method: getAnimations and stylesheet probe under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce
checkOutcomes.evidence: Eight 2-second shimmer animations remained active under reduce and no reduced-motion stylesheet rule was found.
Under prefers-contrast: more, body and primary controls remained visible; Lighthouse separately identified ordinary contrast failures captured under be-inclusive.
Primary navigation is cross-document, but stylesheet inspection found no View Transition support.
No parallax, scrollytelling or other scroll-linked animated experience was present on the representative paths, so there is no scroll animation implementation to assess.
checkOutcomes.reason: No parallax, scrollytelling or other scroll-linked animated experience was present on the representative paths, so there is no scroll animation implementation to assess.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The exercised browsing surfaces use native scrolling and ordinary links rather than custom pointer-drag gesture handlers that fight platform behavior.

checkOutcomes.method: Long-page layout and rendered CSS inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: Long listing page has static chrome and no detected scroll-state/scroll-timeline styling.
No tooltip, anchored menu or edge-positioned popover was opened or required in the representative core flow; the consent surface is modal rather than anchored.
checkOutcomes.reason: No tooltip, anchored menu or edge-positioned popover was opened or required in the representative core flow; the consent surface is modal rather than anchored.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Active navigation is marked with a strong red underline, page headings describe each destination, and the 404 provides an explicit return link.
Fresh desktop loads are covered by the cookie choice overlay before the core content can be used.
Modal-looking consent UI has no dialog element or dialog role in the rendered DOM.
After rejecting consent, the layout gives most remaining area to cards/content; navigation chrome is dense but functional and consistent.
360 px condition reports 1024 px scroll width and 664 px overflow.

checkOutcomes.method: Rendered CSS feature probe and screenshot
checkOutcomes.evidence: No @container rules detected; card/sidebar composition remains fixed in narrow condition.
Focused first visible link has neither outline nor box shadow.
Homepage H1 clearly identifies popular free videos; category, detail and signup surfaces expose direct next actions.

checkOutcomes.method: Representative browse-to-detail and signup branch walkthrough
checkOutcomes.evidence: Homepage links resolve to listing and detail destinations, and the signup email branch opens and reaches validation without a dead end.
Empty signup submission gives two specific Spanish validation messages; unknown route explains failure and links back to the homepage.
Lighthouse LCP 3566.8 ms exceeds good threshold; CLS 0 and TBT 0.
Layout observer and Lighthouse both measured CLS 0 during the observed load, despite missing image dimensions being a future-risk asset hygiene issue.
Trace found two long tasks, longest 179.6 ms, with 157.8 ms TBT; Lighthouse measured 0 ms TBT, indicating acceptable but imperfect main-thread load.

checkOutcomes.method: HAR summary confirmed against live DOM
checkOutcomes.evidence: 141 requests and three confirmed head stylesheets at high parser priority create a broad critical graph.
61 scripts transfer about 1.01 MB; largest bundle is about 402 KB.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse accessibility and DOM form probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse reports missing button/link names and signup email inputs lack labels.
Lighthouse reports 13 color contrast failures.
Landmarks and heading order are sound, but computed keyboard focus indication is absent.
Desktop and narrow screenshots use readable type sizes and clear labels; no text clipping was observed independently of the broader horizontal reflow failure.
360 px viewport has 664 px horizontal overflow and a clipped reading order.
Lighthouse errors-in-console audit returned no items and best-practices score was 1.0.

checkOutcomes.method: DOM document probe and image audit
checkOutcomes.evidence: Doctype/UTF-8 are valid, but 29 images lack intrinsic dimensions and 12 are oversized.
Lighthouse best-practices score is 1.0 with no deprecated API findings; no permission prompt appeared on load.
Homepage has a unique Spanish title and a descriptive meta description in both raw and rendered HTML.
Viewport meta is present, core navigation uses real href links, and robots allows public core routes; mobile layout quality is recorded separately.
Canonical and HTTP 200 pass, but no hreflang and no usable sitemap signal were found.
Video detail has Open Graph metadata but no JSON-LD VideoObject.
HTTPS/HSTS pass, but two cookies are not Secure and CSP only supplies frame-ancestors.

checkOutcomes.method: HAR/tracker capture correlated with first-load screenshot
checkOutcomes.evidence: 117 third-party requests and 1.56 MB occur while consent is unresolved.
No permission prompt appears on load, but exercised signup exposes federated and password routes without a visible passkey option.
HSTS and anti-framing pass; nosniff and Referrer-Policy are absent and Permissions-Policy is not least-privilege.

checkOutcomes.method: Raw HTML/rendered comparison with crawler screenshot
checkOutcomes.evidence: Raw no-JS HTML contains 87% of rendered content words with title, H1 and description present; it is not a JS shell.
Representative lists, consent, signup branch and detail loaded without blank shells; the consent surface remains within the desktop viewport.
Streaming video is intrinsically online for its core task. A minimal-ui manifest exists, but offline playback/installability was judged out of scope rather than required for this media site.
checkOutcomes.reason: Streaming video is intrinsically online for its core task. A minimal-ui manifest exists, but offline playback/installability was judged out of scope rather than required for this media site.

checkOutcomes.evidence: A deliberate unknown route renders a clear Spanish not-found message, support direction, homepage recovery link and useful content.
The document declares lang=es and the interface, errors and metadata are consistently localized; a broad locale switcher is available.
The representative public and signup paths did not expose dates, currency, or locale-sensitive numeric inputs whose formatting could be meaningfully exercised.
checkOutcomes.reason: The representative public and signup paths did not expose dates, currency, or locale-sensitive numeric inputs whose formatting could be meaningfully exercised.

checkOutcomes.evidence: No scheduled event, partial time or user-facing time-zone workflow appeared on the representative paths.
checkOutcomes.reason: No scheduled event, partial time or user-facing time-zone workflow appeared on the representative paths.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Cookie Accept and Reject actions are equally prominent and the signup disclosure states public/partner data use; no preselected paid continuity was encountered.
After empty submission, Spanish messages state that email is required and password needs six characters; validation appears after interaction.
Email inputs use autocomplete=off and lack associated labels.
The representative account-entry flow exposes login, Google, X and email options and clearly states age-verification and data-use consequences before registration.
12 images are oversized and 29 omit dimensions; three have no srcset.
Collector and advertising work is initiated before consent within a 141-request load.
About 94% of 1.67 MB initial transfer is classified third-party before playback.
No declared agent-facing intent exists, and exposing sensitive adult-content actions to autonomous tools would require explicit safety/product design not evidenced here.
checkOutcomes.reason: No declared agent-facing intent exists, and exposing sensitive adult-content actions to autonomous tools would require explicit safety/product design not evidenced here.

checkOutcomes.evidence: No summarisation or language-model task is part of the exercised core browsing/signup journey; absence of on-device inference is not a quality failure here.
checkOutcomes.reason: No summarisation or language-model task is part of the exercised core browsing/signup journey; absence of on-device inference is not a quality failure here.

checkOutcomes.method: Baseline and post-interaction heap summary comparison
checkOutcomes.evidence: After ten repeated scroll/menu-toggle cycles, heap self size rose only 136,732 bytes (0.38%) and node count 0.49%, with no unbounded-growth signal.

checkOutcomes.method: Heap summary and runtime memory metrics
checkOutcomes.evidence: Heap summary reports 36.46 MB self size and runtime probe about 22.96 MB used JS heap for a media-heavy listing, proportionate to the observed page.
Neither heap summary reports Detached constructors among summarized populations; native/object counts remain stable across the repeated interaction.

principleOutcomes.reason: No declared agent-facing intent exists, and exposing sensitive adult-content actions to autonomous tools would require explicit safety/product design not evidenced here. No summarisation or language-model task is part of the exercised core browsing/signup journey; absence of on-device inference is not a quality failure here.
